officialTitle: Abemaciclib Combined With Endocrine Therapy for the Adjuvant Treatment of HR+, HER2-, Node-Positive, High-Risk, Early Breast Cancer (monarchE)

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: At a preplanned efficacy interim analysis, among 5,637 randomly assigned patients, 323 IDFS events were observed in the intent-to-treat population.
design.notes: Cohort 1: ≥4 positive nodes, or 1-3 nodes with grade 3 or tumour ≥5 cm. Cohort 2: 1-3 nodes with Ki-67 ≥20%. Abemaciclib for 2 years with standard endocrine therapy.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding 2 years of abemaciclib to adjuvant endocrine therapy improve invasive disease-free survival in high-risk, node-positive HR+/HER2- early breast cancer?

pico.population: HR+/HER2-, node-positive early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence after surgery (± chemotherapy and radiotherapy)
pico.intervention: Abemaciclib for 2 years plus standard endocrine therapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: IDFS. Secondary: DRFS, OS, safety

arms.label: Abemaciclib + ET
arms.regimen: Abemaciclib plus standard adjuvant endocrine therapy
arms.doseSourceQuote: randomly assigned (1:1) to standard-of-care adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) with or without abemaciclib (150 mg twice daily for 2 years)

publications.title: Adjuvant Abemaciclib Plus Endocrine Therapy for Hormone Receptor-Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative, High-Risk Early Breast Cancer: Results From a Preplanned monarchE Overall Survival Interim Analysis, Including 5-Year Efficacy Outcomes.
publications.label: OS interim analysis including 5-year efficacy outcomes

outcomes.sourceQuote: Abemaciclib plus ET demonstrated superior IDFS versus ET alone (= .01; hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.93), with 2-year IDFS rates of 92.2% versus 88.7%, respectively.

At a median follow-up of 42 months (IQR 37-47), median invasive disease-free survival was not reached in either group and the invasive disease-free survival benefit previously reported was sustained: HR 0·664 (95% CI 0·578-0·762, nominal p<0·0001). At 4 years, the absolute difference in invasive disease-free survival between the groups was 6·4% (85·8% [95% CI 84·2-87·3] in the abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy group vs 79·4% [77·5-81·1] in the endocrine therapy alone group).
157 (5·6%) of 2808 patients in the abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy group died compared with 173 (6·1%) of 2829 patients in the endocrine therapy alone group (HR 0·929, 95% CI 0·748-1·153; p=0·50).

safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (in 548 [19·6%] of 2791 patients receiving abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy vs 24 [0·9%] of 2800 patients in the endocrine therapy alone group), leukopenia (318 [11·4%] vs 11 [0·4%]), and diarrhoea (218 [7·8%] vs six [0·2%]).

The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (in 548 [19·6%] of 2791 patients receiving abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy vs 24 [0·9%] of 2800 patients in the endocrine therapy alone group), leukopenia (318 [11·4%] vs 11 [0·4%]), and diarrhoea (218 [7·8%] vs six [0·2%]).
Serious adverse events occurred in 433 (15·5%) of 2791 patients receiving abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy versus 256 (9·1%) of 2800 receiving endocrine therapy.
There were two treatment-related deaths in the abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy group (diarrhoea and pneumonitis) and none in the endocrine therapy alone group.

strengths: Large randomised phase 3 trial in a clearly defined high-risk population
Benefit sustained and widening beyond the 2-year treatment period
limitations: OS not statistically significant at the reported interim analyses
Diarrhoea and neutropenia require proactive management

clinicalImplications.text: Supports adding 2 years of adjuvant abemaciclib to endocrine therapy for HR+/HER2-, node-positive early breast cancer meeting monarchE high-risk criteria.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The absolute IDFS gain grew after treatment stopped (a carryover effect) — eligibility hinges on nodal burden plus grade, size or Ki-67 as defined in the trial.
